queries.query: the Isha Upanishad's warning that devotion to mere works leads into gloom, devotion to knowledge alone into a gloom deeper still, and that only one who holds the two together passes over death
queries.note: Verses 9-11; 'enter into blind darkness... enter, as it were, into greater darkness' paraphrased to gloom / deeper gloom; 'overcomes death... obtains immortality' compressed. First draft on the Self-in-all-beings verses (6-7) missed top-15 — that theme is corpus-wide (Gita ch V, Eckhart, Rumi came back instead).

queries.query: can a person act in the world for a whole lifetime without being bound by their deeds
queries.note: Verse 2's hundred years of works that do not cling — but the Gita's karma-yoga and taoist non-action answer the same question. No target — graded post-hoc.
